subject: Tokyo / Singapore / Sydney demo — day-wrap availability?
messages:
From: Akira Sato <akira.sato@aquavistahealth.jp>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@aquavistahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 09:10:00 +0900
Subject: Request: Redwood demo for APAC teams

Hi Logan / Marissa,

Thanks for the outreach — we'd love to see Redwood in action. Our product and infra teams are based in Tokyo and Singapore, and APAC leadership in Sydney sometimes joins. Can we schedule a 45m demo in an APAC-friendly window?

Good options for us (local times):
- Tokyo (JST): 09:30–11:00 or 15:00–17:00
- Singapore (SGT): 08:30–10:00 or 14:00–16:00
- Sydney (AEST): 10:30–12:00 or 16:00–18:00

We are mindful of the "day-wrap" — anything after 23:00 JST tends to be next-day for our Sydney folks. Also, FYI, Australia is currently at UTC+11 due to DST.

Tom (cc) will coordinate availability on his side — he prefers mornings SGT but can do the later slot if needed. We can do next week (Dec 7–10) or the week after.

Thanks,
Akira Sato
Head of Platform Ops — AquaVista Health
akira.sato@aquavistahealth.jp
+81 90-1234-5678

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Akira Sato <akira.sato@aquavistahealth.jp>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 18:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Redwood demo for APAC teams

Hi Akira — great to hear, thanks for the detail. Quick question on the window: would Dec 7 at 10:00 AM work for you? I scheduled a tentative slot and attached an invite.

Note: I suggested 10:00 AM PST originally (sorry — I was thinking in my local calendar) but the invite I attached is for 10:00 AM in your local timezone (I double-checked). If that's confusing I can re-send specific times for JST/SGT/AEST.

Proposed (converted) examples:
- Dec 7, 10:00 JST / Dec 7, 09:00 SGT / Dec 7, 12:00 AEST
- Dec 7, 16:00 JST / Dec 7, 15:00 SGT / Dec 7, 18:00 AEST

I'm attaching a short demo brief so you can circulate ahead of time. If the 10:00 JST slot is OK I'll lock it.

Attachments: redwood_apac_demo_invite.ics, apac-demo-brief.pdf

Best,
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Thanks Logan — quick clarification: when you said "Dec 7, 10:00 JST / Dec 7, 09:00 SGT / Dec 7, 12:00 AEST" that actually maps to the same absolute time, but for our Sydney attendees 12:00 AEST is fine. The confusion is that your earlier line about PST made Tom think you meant 10:00 US time and he almost accepted a slot that would have been overnight here.

Can you confirm the invite time zone on the calendar event? Also, for cross-checking, please list the absolute time in UTC in your next message — it helps when we loop in the APAC leadership team who are on different regional calendars.

Would you mind doing two short options in the invite (one morning JST/SGT and one late afternoon JST/SGT) so we can pick without re-emailing? Morning is preferred.

Akira

Heads-up loop for coordination — quick notes:
- Akira asked explicitly for the UTC time in the calendar. Let's avoid ambiguous "10:00" lines.
- I'll shoot two invites: (A) Dec 7, 01:00 UTC (which is Dec 7 10:00 JST / Dec 7 09:00 SGT / Dec 7 12:00 AEST) — morning option
- (B) Dec 7, 07:00 UTC (which is Dec 7 16:00 JST / Dec 7 15:00 SGT / Dec 7 18:00 AEST) — late-afternoon option

I'll include both times as separate events with clear UTC/JST/SGT/AEST labels and mark one tentative. Also adding a one-sheet (attached) that maps the time conversions to avoid further confusion.

Logan — please confirm you're okay with presenting the model performance + cost controls section (15m). Vivek, can you cover routing/fallback (10m)? I'll handle the rollout and SLA bit (10m). That sums to ~35m + 10m Q&A.

- Option B (late APAC): Dec 7, 07:00 UTC — Dec 7 16:00 JST / Dec 7 15:00 SGT / Dec 7 18:00 AEST

Appreciate the patience on the timezone juggling — we run into this a lot with APAC demos and the UTC label seems to reduce back-and-forth.

Cheers,
